Work

What I am working on

Parametric disaster insurance

Jun 2025 – now

Software engineer, DESDR Lab, Columbia Climate School

I model the mechanisms behind disaster insurance for sovereign programmes in Ethiopia, Madagascar and Bangladesh. The instrument is unusual: instead of sending an assessor to count losses, a payout fires automatically when measured conditions cross a threshold agreed in advance. Money arrives in days rather than months.

My side of it is the data engineering. Twenty years of meteorological and satellite records come out of the Google Earth Engine API, through Python and SQL pipelines, and land in a form the models can actually use. On top of that sits the calibration layer that decides where each threshold falls, and the dashboards programme staff use to watch how a change in assumptions moves the number.

I automated the calibration step and cut deployment time by sixty percent. Right now I am coordinating a three-person effort to put the whole Earth Engine ingestion on a secure schedule, replacing a manual download-and-clean cycle with a pipeline that runs unattended and is documented well enough that it does not depend on any one person being around.

Whether models reason or remember

May – Sep 2026

Research intern, Columbia Statistics Department

I ran controlled experiments on whether large language models reason over what they are given or pattern-match their way to an answer that happens to look right. The design held the underlying task fixed while varying what the model could still see in its context, so that recall and reasoning were measured separately instead of scored as one thing.

The harder problem was methodological. A model can look capable because the benchmark quietly rewards memorisation, so I built independent evaluations to separate real performance from statistical artifact before any result was reported.

The gap turned out to be consistent. Recall stayed accurate while reasoning over those same facts fell away once the source left the context window, which the standard benchmarks did not surface. I co-authored the resulting paper with faculty.

Equity research

Jan 2025 – now

Investment analyst, BlackGen Capital

Fundamental research for a nationwide student-run fund: macro conditions paired with company financials, valuation built out in discounted cash flow and comparables. I took a high-conviction position to the investment committee and defended the assumptions and the downside case under questioning, which taught me more than building the model did. It runs alongside everything else now rather than at the centre, though the Python tool I wrote to pull live market data into the workflow is still doing the dull part.

Things I have built

Personal projects

Route Scout

React · TypeScript · Vite · Google Maps API

A trip planner that optimises a day of sightseeing on a live map, weighing stop priority, how long you want at each place, and travel mode. It keeps your itinerary between sessions, recalculates the route as you reorder it, and hands off to turn-by-turn navigation in one tap.

Three-tier web architectureprivate repo

C · TCP/IP sockets · HTTP/1.0 · concurrent I/O

A full stack built from the bottom: a frontend client, a backend database, and a custom HTTP server written to sit between them. Socket-based concurrency for multiple clients at once, fault-tolerant request handling, and protection against directory traversal. Writing a web server by hand is the fastest way to stop treating HTTP as magic.

Quantitative valuation platform

Python · market data APIs

Multi-stage discounted cash flow and cost-of-capital optimisation running against real-time market data, with ratio analysis, beta and volatility handled automatically rather than rebuilt per company.
